description: The floating comment indicator *> (ISO §2023:6.2.3.1) - a comment line when it is the first character-string in the program-text area, an inline comment after one or more character-strings - in either reference format. COBOL-85 had only the fixed comment indicators * and / of the indicator area, so *> in the program text of a COBOL-85 source is not a comment indicator. Recognized in ONE place, the §2023:6.5 logical conversion in ReferenceFormatProcessor (kb/Work PB1493), which gates it once per compilation, in FIXED form - the only reference format a COBOL-85 source can be written in (free form is itself a 2002 introduction, reached below 2002 only through the documented auto-detection extension, and the floating indicator is its only comment); the witness is therefore fixed-form. The edition edge below 2023 is DERIVED, not quoted (VCR row 7.21's discipline - the repo holds no 2002 or 2014 text, ratified decision #1): the M2 post-85 feature catalog in docs/ISO2023_CONFORMANCE_PLAN.md places '*>' inline comments in COBOL-2002, and Annex E, which itemizes the 2014->2023 delta, does not list the floating indicators, so they predate 2023.
citation: ISO §2023:6.2.3.1 (floating indicators, both reference formats); a COBOL-2002 introduction (M2 catalog derivation, VCR row 7.21 discipline)
source:
000100 IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
000200 PROGRAM-ID. PB1493FC.
000300 PROCEDURE DIVISION.
000400 MAIN.
000500     DISPLAY "X". *> an inline comment
000600     STOP RUN.
